chunks: I heard Abu al-Hasan Musa ibn Ja'far (peace be upon him) — we were seated with him in the Mosque of the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) — we discussed the matter of women and engaged extensively in the topic, while he remained silent, not entering our conversation with a single word.

When we fell silent, he said: 'As for free women, do not mention them. But the best of slave girls is the one toward whom you have desire, and she possesses intellect and good manners, so you need not command or prohibit her.'

Below that is one toward whom you have desire but she lacks good manners, so you need to command and prohibit. Below her is one toward whom you have desire but she has neither intellect nor good manners; you endure patience with her because of your passion for her. And a slave girl toward whom you have no desire, and she has neither intellect nor good manners — place the green ocean between yourself and her.

He (the narrator) said: So I grabbed my beard, wanting to make a derisive sound at our excessive discussion since we had not arrived at any conclusion, and at his comprehensive statement. He then said to me: 'Enough! If you do that, I will not sit with you.'

key_terms.أدب: Moral comportment, good manners, refined conduct
key_terms.البحر الأخضر: The green ocean — proverbial expression for extreme separation or an unbridgeable distance
key_terms.الجواري: Slave girls/concubines — discussed within the context of Islamic laws governing concubinage
key_terms.الحرائر: Free women — the Imam directs that they should not be the subject of men's idle conversation
key_terms.عقل: Intellect, reason — the capacity for rational self-governance
key_terms.هوى: Desire, affection, inclination — the emotional component of the relationship

ai.seo_question: What did Imam Musa al-Kazim say about the types of slave girls and free women?
ai.summary: In the Prophet's mosque, Imam Musa al-Kazim (AS) listened silently while his companions engaged in an excessive discussion about women. When they fell silent, the Imam prohibited speaking about free women (harair) entirely, then categorized slave girls (jawari) into four types based on intellect (aql), good manners (adab), and the owner's personal affection (hawa). This narration reflects the Imam's dignified silence as a form of pedagogical control, followed by a concise, practical taxonomy that reveals his concern for the rights and treatment of women in Islamic household law. The narrator's self-deprecating response and the Imam's firm rebuke further underscore the seriousness of the teaching.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ali Bin Asbaat, from Muhammad Bin Al Sabbah, from Abdul Rahman Bin Al Hajjaj, from Abdullah Bin Mus’ab Al Zubeyri who said, 
‘I heard Abu Al-Hassan Musa<sup>asws</sup> Bin Ja’far<sup>asws</sup>, and we were seated with him<sup>asws</sup> in the Masjid of Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup>, so we mentioned the matter of the women. So we discussed a lot and he<sup>asws</sup> was silent, not entering in our discussion with a single word.

So when we were silent, he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘As for the free ones, so you should not be mentioning them, but the best of the slave girls is the one whom you love and for her is an intellect, and manners, so you would neither be needy to instruct her nor prohibit her.

And lower than that is the one whom you love but she does not have oral discipline and you need to command and prohibit; and lower than her is the one whom you do not love and there is no intellect for her nor any manners, so you observe patience upon her in place of your passion regarding her; and a slave girl for whom there is no passion for you regarding her, and there is no intellect for her, nor any manners, so you should make the green ocean to be between you and her’.

He (the narrator) said, ‘So I grabbed my beard intending that I make a loud sound (via mouth an arrogant/stupid call) because of the abundance of our discussion and not standing therein upon anything, and due to his<sup>asws</sup> comprehensive speech’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said to me: ‘Shh! If you do it, I would not sit with you’.
en.sarwar: 2. A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Ali ibn Asbat from Muhammad ibn al-Sabbah from ‘Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj from ‘Abd Allah ibn Mus’ab al-Zubayriy who has said the following: “I once I heard abu al-Hassan, Musa ibn Ja‘far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam - while we were sitting in the Masjid of the Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause - discussing issues about women and we delved in it a great deal but he (the Imam) was quiet and did not enter in our discussion not even with one word;

but when we became quiet then I heard him (the Imam) saying, ‘As far as free ones are concerned you must not speak about them, however, the best slave-girl is one whom you love, who has power of reason and moral discipline so you do not need to command or prohibit.

Next to this is the one whom you love but does not have moral discipline and you need to command and prohibit. Next to this is the one whom you love but who does not have the power of reason and moral discipline and you have to exercise patience because of your love. Next to this is the slave-girl whom you do not love, she does not have the power of reason or moral discipline and you keep between yourself and her, the green ocean.’

He (the narrator) has said, ‘I then held my beard and wanted to make the sound of loud flatus because of our so much delving and without reaching any meaningful point and for his comprehensive words. He (the Imam) said, ‘Hold it, if you did it I will not sit with you.’”
